page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-allocated virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 13.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1105.58, and the multi-core score is 1452.88, both categorized as weak to poor. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.89 GB/sec for cached reads and 13.32 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Geekbench results align with these findings, yielding a single-core score of 944.0 and a multi-core score of 1124.0. Static web serving throughput is measured at 1.58 GB/sec, while small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model achieves 37.16 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-highmem-2 offers a qualitative advantage for workloads requiring more memory than compute power without the premium of newer-generation architectures. However, the tradeoff is lower raw CPU performance and memory bandwidth. This profile is best suited for lightweight memory-bound workloads, small databases, caching layers, and basic web serving where high CPU throughput is not a primary requirement.
